author: blu
body: A revised field's value is hoisted into a let so that every value is computed BEFORE the first __record-set mutates the record in place -- without that, a later field's expression would read the already-mutated record. The hoist is not optional.

author: blu
body: So the ARGUMENT is hoisted and the __narrow stays at the store: `let __rv0 = n in __record-set __rev "f" (__narrow __rv0)`. The value is still computed before any mutation, so the ordering the hoist exists for is untouched; __narrow is a pure range assertion on an already-computed value, so moving it one step later asserts the same thing about the same value. The marker survives to the check that looks for it.

author: blu
body: An act block took `synthetic-span`, which is 0,0, and the CST `ActExpr` carries no token of its own to take a position from. That made it the one AST node standing exactly where the most common effect error lands: `check-def` reports CDX2031 against `aexpr-span (def.body)`, and for any def whose body is an act block -- most effectful code in the language -- that span was 0,0 and the diagnostic printed with no line:column at all. Not a wrong position, an absent one.

author: blu
body: The statements inside DO carry spans (a bind takes its token's, an expression statement its expression's), so the block takes its first statement's. That is a real position inside the block rather than a guess, and an empty block keeps `synthetic-span` because there is nothing truthful to point at.

author: blu
body: These two are per-definition loops, and per-definition is the grain the DESUGAR deck grows at: every definition's whole expression tree is rebuilt on the deck. deck-room-left answers whether another definition fits, and a loop that runs out stops where it is. The chapter it was building is thrown away by desugar-document rather than returned truncated -- see the note there.

author: blu
body: deck-out-of-room answers True once the deck is within a guard band of its reservation's top. A ceiling of zero means unbounded, which is what a caller with no reservation of its own passes -- the same convention tokenize-collect uses.

author: blu
body: The saturation test is taken AFTER the loops and BEFORE the chapter is assembled, and the truncated work is then discarded rather than returned. Both halves matter. Returning the partial chapter would assemble a record whose lists cost eight bytes per surviving definition on the very deck that just refused another definition, which is how the LEX guard shipped with a hole: firing is not the job if the wind-down walks through the ceiling anyway. Nothing downstream wants this chapter -- the caller raises CDX9002 on dr-sat and the bag carries an error from there on.

author: blu
body: synth-class-type-defs gives a class with a superclass an extra dictionary field, __super-<Super> of type <Super>Dict. Nothing ever put a value in it. The instance dictionary was built from the instance's methods alone, so the field was left to __alloc, which zero-fills -- a superclass dictionary that was a null pointer in every instance of every class that had one.

author: blu
body: An instance of a class with a superclass now names the superclass's dictionary for the same type. If that instance does not exist, <Super>-dict-<Type> is an undefined name and the compiler says so, which is the honest answer to an unsatisfied superclass constraint.
